subject: Discovery: model parity criteria & next steps (NovusFin)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: model parity criteria & next steps (NovusFin)

Hi Liam / NovusEval team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clear description of the two core P0s you need:
- 1) factual/financial reasoning correctness (quarterly-report style Q&A)
- 2) consolidation latency under 350ms median per token in production.

Quick recap and proposals so we all line up before the technical trial:
1) Recommended models to trial (initial batch):
   - redwood-open-3b-q4f16 (fast, quantized; good latency profile)
   - redwood-open-7b-compat (strong on multi-step reasoning in our internal evals)
   - baseline-enterprise-v1 (your current in-house baseline — we'll run side-by-side)

2) Acceptance / parity guidance (proposed):
   - Accuracy parity: open model score no more than -3 percentage points on the Financial QA F1 compared to baseline on your prompt set.
   - Safety/ hallucination: factuality score drop limited to <= 4% absolute.
   - Latency: p50 per-token <= 350ms; p95 <= 700ms in dedicated config.
   - Edge-case gating: any regression on the 12 critical regulatory prompts must be addressed before canary.

3) Deliverables we attached to this thread:
   - novusfin-eval-prompts-v2.txt (prompt set subset you asked for)
   - novusfin-benchmark-summary-20260825.csv (our run on your prompts vs baseline)
   - mutual-action-plan-novusfin.pdf (draft M.A.P with timeline & responsibilities)

4) Next steps (ask of NovusFin):
   - Confirm the acceptance thresholds above or propose adjustments by EOD Wed 8/1.
   - Share any additional red-team prompts you want included for hallucination checks.
   - Confirm preferred window for a controlled load run (we suggest Sep 2–4).

Marissa will follow up with a short technical commentary on the benchmarks (attached) and proposed eval scripts. Rafael is looped for any capacity/ops questions.

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30m alignment next week to lock the M.A.P.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- The "Financial QA F1" you reference — can you confirm the exact metric and eval harness you used (precision/recall weighting)? We have a couple of legacy scripts and want to make sure we're comparing apples-to-apples.
- For latency: our 350ms p50 target is end-to-end for a single conversational turn on our production infra (including request routing). If the per-token figure is lower, we can map it — please propose a transformation or formula we can verify in our runs.
- Regulatory prompts: we will send 5 additional compliance prompts by Monday that must be included in the gating.

Also — is running the "redwood-open-7b-compat" model in a dedicated config expected to meet our latency SLOs, or would that require quantization and batch tuning? We prefer a config that is realistic to run in our pre-prod.

Happy to hop on a short call Tue morning if that helps.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, ML Ops — NovusFin
liam.oconnor@novusfin.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novusfin.com>, ops+eval@novusfin.com
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: model parity criteria & next steps (NovusFin)

Liam — short technical notes to align the eval harness and proposed thresholds.

1) Metric specifics:
   - The Financial QA F1 we used is the canonical span-based F1 over ground-truth spans (scoring both exact and partial matches). Our harness weights precision and recall equally. I attached the small eval script snippets to the Drive link in the M.A.P.

2) Mapping per-token -> end-to-end latency:
   - Our runs report model-side per-token latencies. To approximate your end-to-end p50, use: end_to_end_p50 ~= model_p50 * average_tokens_per_turn * routing_multiplier. Example with your mean token count (45) and routing multiplier 1.12 gives realistic numbers. We can instrument a remote probe during the pre-prod run to get a direct mapping.

3) Results highlights from the attached CSV (summary):
   - redwood-open-3b-q4f16: Financial QA F1 = 86.1% (baseline-enterprise-v1 = 89.8%) — delta = -3.7pp
   - redwood-open-7b-compat: Financial QA F1 = 88.9% — delta = -0.9pp
   - Hallucination/factuality (sampled): open-3b had a 6.1% hallucination rate on long-form reconciliation prompts (above our 4% soft threshold).

4) Recommendation:
   - Run a focused pre-prod trial with redwood-open-7b-compat first (best candidate for parity), and also include the 3b-q4 variant as a low-cost fallback in traffic shaping.
   - Define explicit regression gates on the 12 regulatory prompts and the 5 compliance prompts you’ll send. Any fail on those prompts requires a root-cause and mitigation (prompt engineering, eval-based postprocessing, or model variant swap) before canary.

5) Ops notes (Rafael):
   - Rafael: can you confirm whether we can provision a dedicated 7b-compat cluster with quantized weights for the Sep 2–4 window? Also need guidance on network routing multiplier to be conservative.

Happy to run a short demo of the harness and walk through the CSV on Tue.

— Marissa
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
